_note: Core/Device (parity/F06-device.md), the DEVICE YEAR CLASS fold. A COARSE performance bucket from physical memory and core count, not a benchmark and not a claim about the release date of a specific device. It exists so an app can drop a blur, a particle field or a heavy shader on old hardware in ONE condition, which is the alternative to a device allowlist that rots. Pinned because three renderers compute it and a silent divergence would make the same phone fast on one platform and slow on another. The ladder is memory first (it is the fact that actually predicts whether a heavy surface survives) with the core count breaking the top bucket only.
_runner: No runner is wired yet (registration is in the F06 handoff). Implemented identically as Device.yearClass in swift/, kotlin/ and web/.

cases.name: 8 GB with 8 cores is the current bucket
8 GB with fewer cores is one step back
the boundaries sit BELOW the round number, because a device reporting 8 GB never reports exactly 8589934592
a device just under a boundary lands in the lower bucket
